R0220.title: Virtual World Economic Manipulation
R0220.definition: Attackers manipulate metaverse economic systems by hoarding virtual land, monopolizing virtual currency, causing speculative bubbles.

references.title: Security risks in metaverse economic systems

R0220.description:
Virtual world economic manipulation uses hoarding, virtual currency manipulation, fake volume, or control of scarce resources to influence market prices. Attackers can cash out, launder value, or lure users into speculative bubbles.

When virtual economies connect to real money, advertising revenue, or benefit distribution, manipulation creates financial and consumer protection risk. Platforms need anomaly monitoring across accounts, funds, and market concentration.
R0220.influence: Virtual economy manipulation can inflate asset bubbles, enable cash-out or laundering, and harm users who rely on platform markets.

observables: A few related accounts concentrate holdings of virtual scarce assets and show coordinated trading
Virtual-currency prices show anomalous movements with fake volume absent external bullish news
Related-account groups cash out at highs leaving retail-bag-holder patterns
Key resources in the virtual economy are monopolized by a single entity or ring
Anomalous trades concentrate on channels convertible to real funds accompanied by money-laundering signatures
